title: Spain Beats Argentina 1-0 in Extra Time to Win 2026 World Cup
detail: Substitute Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute as Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, NJ) to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup — Spain's second title, and first since 2010. A sellout crowd of 80,663 watched Argentina fail to register a single shot on target across 90 minutes of regulation, finishing with just two shots and 0.2 expected goals to Spain's 20 shots and 1.94 xG. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez set a World Cup final record with 11 saves to keep Argentina level into extra time. Argentina's Fernández was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time. It may have been Lionel Messi's final World Cup appearance; he was seen in tears on the pitch afterward, later posting: 'The pain is immense and it will take time for this wound to heal... I'll also take away all the good things.' Referee: Slavko Vinčić (Slovenia). President Trump and FIFA president Gianni Infantino presented the trophy.

media.caption: Ferran Torres celebrates his extra-time winner as Spain beats Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final

title: Rodri Wins Golden Ball; Mbappé Takes Golden Boot for Second Straight World Cup
detail: FIFA's Technical Study Group named Spain midfielder Rodri winner of the adidas Golden Ball as the tournament's best player, with Argentina captain Lionel Messi finishing second (Silver Ball) and France's Kylian Mbappé third (Bronze Ball). Mbappé won the Golden Boot with 10 goals — becoming the first player to win the award in consecutive World Cups (2022 and 2026) — with Messi runner-up on 8 goals. Spain goalkeeper Unai Simón won the Golden Glove, and 19-year-old Spain defender Pau Cubarsí won the Best Young Player award. The sweep gave Spain three of the tournament's four major individual honors, alongside the trophy itself.
